subject: Recap + pricing model for prefix caching impact (next steps)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Grant <ellie@fintechhq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + pricing model for prefix caching impact (next steps)

Thanks again for your time earlier, Ellie — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and a short worked example of how prefix caching changes the effective $/1M user tokens. I want to confirm a couple of numbers so we can lock a pilot price for the POC.

Call recap (3 bullets):
- Primary use case: in-product assistant for transaction categorization and follow-up suggestions; heavy reuse of shared system prompts and user metadata (high prefix re-use expected).
- Current target: keep effective inference spend below $4.00 per 1M user tokens (you said $4 is a stretch target; please confirm).
- Ask from Redwood: confirm expected monthly active users and average prompt/response token lengths so we can finalize the model/quantization recommendation.

Quick worked example (numbers illustrative — I attached the spreadsheet with the full model):
- Raw user tokens (monthly): 100,000 prompts \u00d7 average 200 tokens total (50 user prompt + 150 model output) = 20,000,000 user tokens/month.
- List price for candidate model variant (q4_1 medium-latency): $6.00 per 1M billable tokens (this is the list price used in the example).

Scenario math (how prefix hit rate affects effective $/1M user tokens):
- No cache (0% hit): billable tokens = 20M -> cost = 20 \u00d7 $6 = $120 -> effective $/1M user tokens = $6.00
- Moderate prefix hit (30% hit): billable tokens = 20M \u00d7 (1 - 0.30) = 14M -> cost = 14 \u00d7 $6 = $84 -> effective $/1M user tokens = $4.20
- High prefix hit (45% hit): billable tokens = 11M -> cost = $66 -> effective $/1M user tokens = $3.30

Notes on assumptions:
- "Prefix hit" refers to cases where the KV/prefix cache returns partial or complete cached token sequences and those tokens are not billed again. We modeled cacheable portion = shared system prompts + user metadata chunk (roughly 40-60 tokens per request in our sample).
- Billing model: Redwood bills on billable tokens (tokens the runtime actually decodes); prefix/cache hits reduce billable tokens but not the user-visible token counts used above.

Questions for you to confirm (so we can finalize a pilot price):
1) Is the monthly volume above closer to 20M user tokens or higher (e.g., 50M)?
2) Typical prompt/response split — does 50 tokens prompt / 150 tokens output match reality?
3) Do you have an internal expectation for prefix reuse (e.g., percent of requests sharing the same 50-150 token prefix)?

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm volumes, we will run a quick traffic replay (1 week) against staging to estimate real prefix hit and produce a refined effective $/1M.
- Pilot proposal: 6-week pilot with capped spend and interim monthly checkpoint; we can set a conditional pilot price once we have replay numbers.

I've attached the token-modeling workbook with the three scenarios and a short one-pager on prefix cache behavior.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — useful writeup. A few clarifications from our side:
- MAU and usage: ~50k MAU (monthly), we expect ~2 interaction events per user per month for the assistant (so ~100k prompts/month).
- Token characteristics: average user prompt ~40-60 tokens, model output ~120-180 tokens. Your 50/150 split is reasonable.
- That gives approx: 100k prompts \u00d7 200 tokens = 20M user tokens/month (your number aligns).
- Target price: we'd like to target <= $4.00 per 1M user tokens for the steady state (pilot can be higher if we demonstrate hit rates).

Can you confirm: what list price model/quantization gives the best chance to get to sub-$4.00 with a realistic cache hit (we expect 25-35% initially)? Also please send any sample replay instrumentation we need to share to run the prefix analysis on our events.

Attaching our data export spec for a short replay sample.

Best,

ellie@fintechhq.com

- Conservative vs optimistic prefix hit assumptions and resulting effective $/1M (include scenario numbers).
- Any engineering pre-reqs for the replay (format of event export, sample size).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + pricing model for prefix caching impact (next steps)

Quick technical/commercial readout based on their numbers and our recent pilots: 

1) Recommended model variant and list price
- Recommend q4_1-medium (good latency / cost balance) \u2013 list price for modeling: $6.00 per 1M billable tokens.

2) Prefix cache assumptions (realistic baseline for replay)
- Conservative baseline: 20% prefix hit (early pilot, low reuse)
- Expected baseline: 30% prefix hit (reasonable for shared system prompts + metadata reuse)
- Optimistic: 45%+ (after tweak: client-side prefix canonicalization + SDK sticky cache)
- Cacheable token estimate: on average 50 tokens per request (system prompt + metadata).

3) Effective pricing math (using Ellie's ~20M user tokens):
- No cache (0%): billable = 20M -> cost = 20 \u00d7 $6 = $120 -> effective = $6.00 /1M user tokens
- Conservative (20% hit): billable = 16M -> cost = 16 \u00d7 $6 = $96 -> effective = $4.80 /1M
- Expected (30% hit): billable = 14M -> cost = $84 -> effective = $4.20 /1M
- Optimistic (45% hit): billable = 11M -> cost = $66 -> effective = $3.30 /1M

4) Pilot commercial proposal (what Sales should offer)
- Offer a conditional pilot price of $4.50 per 1M user tokens for the 6-week pilot with a spend cap of $5k, with the condition we run the traffic replay in week 1 and share observed prefix hit. If observed hit >=30%, we convert pilot invoice to $4.00 per 1M for steady-state (retroactive credit applied to pilot invoice up to the spend cap).

5) Engineering pre-reqs for replay
- Send ~7 days of anonymized request/response pairs (JSONL) or 1 week sampled stream (~5-10k requests) with prompt + response tokens and session id. We will run replay against staging and produce prefix hit distribution and recommended cache TTL.

6) Next internal steps (owners / timeline)
- Ben: set up replay environment and sample script (ETA 48 hours).
- Marissa: draft MAP + pilot SOW and pricing term (ETA Thu EOD PT).
- Diego: confirm commercial ask with Ellie and schedule kick-off meeting (ETA today).

I'll prepare a short summary slide for the pilot pricing and include the effective $/1M math so we can be transparent with the customer.

--
